title: I've been building a god simulator with Claude Code, and it's turned into a pretty ambitious project
author: Dependent-Block-1319
selftext:
Hey!

I've been working on a game called GODSHIFT, a god simulator where civilizations evolve independently in a living sandbox world.

I've been using Claude Code to help with programming, debugging, and implementing some of the more complex systems.

I handle the game design, ideas, testing, and decisions about how everything should work.

What started as a relatively simple civilization simulation has grown into something much bigger.

There are individual inhabitants, evolving kingdoms, diplomacy, wars, pirates, dinosaurs, natural disasters, and even a giant Kraken.

One of the biggest challenges has been making all these systems interact while keeping the simulation running smoothly, especially when populations grow.

It's definitely been a learning experience, and there's still a lot I want to improve.

I've released the current Windows version on itch.io for $4.99 https://fanfan77.itch.io/godshift

I'm curious if anyone else here is using Claude Code for simulation-heavy games. How are you handling performance and complex AI behaviors?

comments.author: ledniv
comments.body:
Looks super cool!  
  
For simulation-heavy games like this, I’ve found the biggest win is making the **simulation data-first** rather than letting every inhabitant/kingdom own a bunch of scripts and logic. Keep things like position, faction, health, current action, target, etc. in arrays, and process the relevant groups in batches. That helps a lot once populations grow because the CPU spends less time jumping between scattered objects and waiting on memory.

I also try to give Claude Code those architecture rules up front, instead of letting it invent a different pattern for every new system. I made a free Unity Claude Code skill that teaches this Data-Oriented Design approach and can review generated code for violations:

[https://github.com/Data-Oriented-Design-for-Games/unity-data-oriented-design-skills](https://github.com/Data-Oriented-Design-for-Games/unity-data-oriented-design-skills)

I also have a language-agnostic version: [https://github.com/Data-Oriented-Design-for-Games/data-oriented-design](https://github.com/Data-Oriented-Design-for-Games/data-oriented-design)

Small plug: the architecture/performance ideas behind the skill are what I cover in *High Performance Unity Game Development with Data-Oriented Design*:

[https://www.manning.com/books/high-performance-unity-game-development](https://www.manning.com/books/high-performance-unity-game-development)
